newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe hopes Mandela will unlock trade talks jam.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe hopes Mandela will unlock trade talks jam.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Monday makes his first official visit to Zimbabwe, which is hoping he will unblock protracted trade negotiations between the two neighbours.
The Zimbabwe government expects Mandela's talks with President Robert Mugabe to be dominated by discussions on a new trade pact between southern Africa's largest economies.
"The two leaders will look at the modalities of expediting the early conclusion of the trade agreement between Zimbabwe and South Africa," said a government statement announcing the visit.
But South Africa's department of foreign affairs in a statement ahead of the visit eschewed specific mention of the negotiations.
The statement merely said the two leaders would tackle bilateral and regional issues,
Mandela will be accompanied by Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo and his director-general Rusty Evans.

Negotiations to update an expired 1964 trade agreement have gone on since 1992. Zimbabwe's industry and commerce minister Nathan Shamuyarira is on record accusing South Africa of dragging its feet in concluding the agreement.

South Africa is Zimbabwe's largest trading partner in Africa but the trade is heavily weighted in South Africa's favour. In 1995, total trade between the two nations totalled Z$10 billion (U.S.$885 million).
During the visit from May 19 to 21, Mandela is expected to become the first foreign head of state to address the Zimbabwean parliament.
He is also due to attend the World Economic Forum-organised Southern Africa investment summit where more than 500 business executives are expected.
